title: Ops Utility SDK and Replayable Sandbox Catalog
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight Ops Utility SDK and a registry of replayable sandboxes that let support engineers run verified runbook steps as permissioned, idempotent microflows. This ticket covers the API surface, a CLI prototype, a web dry-run visualizer, and the initial sandbox catalog entries for common incident classes (quota exhaustion, KV cache invalidation, model-fallback verification).

Why: Current runbook execution is ad-hoc (ad-hoc scripts + copy-paste). We need reproducible, auditable, and safe runbook execution that: 1) can run in a limited permission sandbox, 2) can be dry-run visualized with synthetic inputs, and 3) can be replayed against production with guardrails and automatic rollback.

Scope (this ticket):
- Design & implement Admin Utility SDK core (python + node clients) with step adapters (http, k8s, sql, opsctl).
- Define runbook-as-data schema (YAML/JSON) with explicit side-effect declarations and compensating steps.
- Implement a Sandbox Runner (ephemeral container + network policy + permission shim) and the dry-run visualizer in Console.
- Populate initial sandbox catalog (5 canonical playbooks) and add telemetry hooks for suggestion engine.

Out of scope: full RBAC integration across Private deployments (follow-up ticket), long-term audit retention policy changes.
acceptance_criteria: Public API for Admin Utility SDK with create/run/dryrun/rollback endpoints and client examples in Python and Node
Runbook-as-data spec published in Docs (confluence) with examples for at least 5 incident classes
Sandbox Runner prototype that spins ephemeral K8s Pods with network egress restricted and a permission shim limiting write scopes
Dry-run visualizer implemented in Console that shows step-by-step state transitions and predicted side-effects
E2E test harness that runs two catalog sandboxes in CI against a staging cluster and asserts no persisted side-effects
Telemetry hooks emit structured events for every sandbox execution (start/finish/step-fail/rollback) visible in Console traces
